title: Fixed Folded Leaves and Integral Stair Bridge Card
description: One newly authored complete fixed paper-cut stair-bridge card. A single continuous finite-thickness paper-like material body forms a broad lower leaf and an upright rear leaf at a right angle. A genuine central cut window removes material across their joined corner, while one thin three-step bridge rises from the front lower margin to the upper window edge. Three genuine rectangular cutouts pierce the thin riser sheets while preserving their full surrounding material borders. Each full tread and windowed riser is materially joined to the next and both terminal ends share the surrounding whole card body, with real open space below and beside the bridge. All outward, inward and cut-thickness faces form one shared-vertex connected closed mesh; this is not a solid block of stairs laid on a card, separate steps glued to an old book or a painted cut line. The complete numeric cut-window, thin plate union and stepped return organization is new. Unlike the older V-fold gatehouse book, there are no thick covers, page blocks, independent facade panels, arch silhouette or added foot tabs. Unlike the concertina book, there is no repeated standing zigzag leaf between separate end boards. No old book, stair, facade, card or mesh fragment imported or extracted. One original model zero scenes; one closed editable whole mesh with four opaque constant untextured PBR face roles, metre-style native Z up, full horizontal-bounds-centred ground datum. Generic blank papercraft illustration with invented proportions and deliberately exaggerated finite sheet thickness, not an artist design, cutting template or physically foldable mechanism. Only this fixed display pose is modeled; no unfolding, closure, flat-pattern mapping, paper elasticity, scoring, real cut manufacture, load, durability or handling safety capability made or verified. No text, decorative motifs, human, rigging, animation or interaction.
